questions.text: Determine the theoretical barrier height, built-in potential barrier, and maximum electric field in a metal–semiconductor diode for zero applied bias.
Repeat Example 9.2 for the GaAs diode capacitance data shown in Figure 9.3.

Consider an ideal chromium-to-n-type silicon Schottky diode at T = 300 K. Assume the semiconductor is doped at a concentration of N_{d} = 3 \times 10^{15} \, \text{cm}^{-3}. Determine the (a) ideal Schottky barrier height, (b) built-in potential barrier, (c) peak electric field with an applied reverse-biased voltage of V_{x} = 5 \, \text{V}, and (d) junction capacitance per unit area for V_{x} = 5 \, \text{V}.
